subject: How a coding Agent expresses reviewed domain facts in code

scenarios.situation: The first external system arrives in a Context that has none.
judged: The application reaches the provider through something named in the domain's language, not the provider's or the transport's.
The provider's protocol, credentials and status vocabulary appear in one place.
A test shows that a delivery failure leaves the Order confirmed.
A test shows that an Order that fails to confirm issues no Receipt.
The stand-in used by the tests and the real sender are held to the same expectations.
The report says what was not verified, including that the real provider was never called.

scenarios.situation: A rule is added where a helper already does part of the work and nothing external is involved.
judged: The thresholds and rates carry names from the domain's language.
No indirection is added that has one implementation and no external system behind it.
The tests sit on the thresholds and one Order below them.

scenarios.situation: A refactoring that must preserve behaviour, where some rules have no test.
judged: Extracted names are the domain's terms for the rules.
The rules stated once for every Service are written once.
The code is not split into functions that only forward to another function.
No extracted function returns its result by changing an argument.
The report states how preserved behaviour was shown, and names any rule that had no test before the change.
The report shows that a test was seen to fail when a rule was broken.

scenarios.situation: The task asks for the project's quality standards and the repository enforces none.
judged: The report says that the repository has no automated standard to check against.
The report claims no numeric threshold or named style guide as the project's standard.
No tool or configuration is introduced to create a standard nobody asked for.

scenarios.situation: A mechanical change inside a reviewed boundary.
judged: No design record, handoff or Registry change is produced.
The report is proportionate to the change.

scenarios.situation: A lint check forbids flag arguments, and the flag selects a set of values that is a domain concept.
judged: What the flag selected is named from the domain's terms, and the functions read that concept instead of asking yes or no.
No value is wrapped in a new type, or in an enum, that is still only asked yes or no.
No flag survives as a keyword argument or a default.
A third kind of Borrower could be added without touching the functions that compute a Loan Quote.

scenarios.situation: A lint check limits the number of arguments, and some of the arguments form a domain concept.
judged: Any new type is a concept named in the domain's terms, and its fields are read where they are used.
The Address rules are stated once, on something named Address, so that pricing a return can reuse them.
No object exists only to carry arguments into one function.
No function only forwards to another.
The check's configuration is unchanged.

scenarios.situation: A lint check forbids literals in comparisons, and the same limits also appear in messages and slices.
judged: Each limit is named from the domain's terms and stated once, and every place it appears, messages included, uses that name.
No constant's name repeats its value.
The report does not claim the change is done because the check passes; it says where else the limits appeared.
